cli_result.result:
**Definition check — passed.** The "Reproducibility" section is present in my instructions and reads as expected. Quoted verbatim and in full:

> Repeatability must be measured on unchanged records under the same evaluator model and definition, because even a fixed or zero sampling temperature does not guarantee identical semantic judgements.

I could not independently verify the sha256 of the definition on disk (no `.claude/agents/` tree exists in this working directory — only `data/rubric`, `input`, `scripts`, `src`), so the supplied digest is recorded as given rather than confirmed.

## Evaluation complete — CHORUS, claudecode_agent, rep3

**Validation:** `VALID output_evaluation.json: rubric20-semantic`, exit 0.

**Score: 67/88 = 76.1%** (fixed and normalized coincide — all 20 questions resolved as applicable, `excluded_max_points: 0`).

| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| Structural Completeness | 19/21 |
| Metadata Quality & Content | 18/21 |
| Technical Documentation | 16/25 |
| FAIRness & Accessibility | 14/21 |

**Applicability.** No question was excluded. Each conditional gate was resolved on fields outside the question's own scoring set, per the anti-circular rule: Q8/Q15 on `description` and `collection_mechanisms` (critically ill patients, ICU/PICU/NICU admissions); Q11 on `external_resources`' chorus-ai GitHub reference; Q10/Q12/Q13/Q17 on `third_party_sharing.is_shared: true` plus populated `distribution_formats`. Access requires approval, which the ambiguity rule directs toward `applicable: true`.

**Shape of the record.** Technically excellent, ethically thin. Standards work is the strongest dimension — five modalities each on the correct community standard, explicit schema URI, admission-level cross-modal linkage (Q10 = 5) — and the funding block validates cleanly (OT2OD032701 matches NIH activity/institute/digit structure, RePORTER path matches the stated application ID). Against that, the human-subjects protections are absent as a block: no `human_subject_research` determination, no IRB, no consent or waiver, and `at_risk_populations` empty despite `subpopulations` itself naming neonatal and pediatric admissions. That last one is a genuine internal contradiction, not merely a missing field.

Three further scored findings worth surfacing: no versioning at all for a release the record says is actively growing (Q13 = 2); `known_biases` entirely empty while a selection-bias statement with mitigation already sits under `known_limitations`, so the content exists but not where a RAI consumer reads it (Q20 = 2); and no demographics of any kind despite demographics being held as an OMOP data type (Q15 = 3).

I did not penalize the record for its extensive `source_caveats`. They are correct practice — the gaps are attributed to the source bundle rather than papered over — but disclosure documents an absence without supplying the missing protection, so the gaps still scored.

**Recorded:** 15 semantic issues (3 high, all human-subjects related), 20 consistency checks passed / 6 failed / 7 warnings; `doi_format: not_present`, `grant_number_format: valid_nih`, `url_validity: some_invalid` (one schemeless external URL; a published contact email carries an apparent upstream domain typo transcribed "as published"). Model recorded as `claude-opus-5` for both `name` and `evaluator_model`, `temperature: null`.
